sentences.text: The name Cryodrakon translates to 'cold dragon' in Greek, while the species name boreas honors the Greek god of the north winds.
This extinct azhdarchid pterosaur, meaning 'cold dragon of the north wind,' lived in what is now Canada during the Late Cretaceous.
The only known species within this genus is Cryodrakon boreas.
Most known fossils belong to young or subadult individuals, suggesting a minimum wingspan of about 5 meters.
A juvenile specimen with a 10.6 mm fifth cervical vertebra was estimated to have a wingspan of about 2 meters.
Cryodrakon is estimated to have had a wingspan of about 10 meters, making it one of the largest flying animals in history.
A large incomplete neck vertebra measuring 40 cm suggests that adult Cryodrakon could have had a vertebra at least 50 cm long.
One researcher even considered 'viserion' as a species name, referencing the ice dragon from Game of Thrones.
Cryodrakon boreas was named and described in 2019 by paleontologists David Hone, Michael Habib, and François Therrien.
The holotype specimen TMP 1992.83 was found in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta in 1992.
Cryodrakon likely hunted smaller animals on the ground, similar to modern marabou storks.
The holotype skeleton showed evidence of being scavenged by a dromaeosaurid, possibly Saurornitholestes langstoni.
A broken tooth found in a Cryodrakon bone suggests its thin-walled bones were very tough.
A 2025 study found probable bite marks on a juvenile Cryodrakon vertebra from various possible predators or scavengers.
Cryodrakon is classified within the pterosaur family Azhdarchidae, which includes Quetzalcoatlus.
Later studies placed Cryodrakon within the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae, though its exact position varies between analyses.
Cryodrakon lived in what is now Canada during the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 76.7 to 74.3 million years ago.
Fossils come from the Dinosaur Park Formation, which preserves alluvial and coastal plain environments.

Researchers noted features that exclude Cryodrakon from a basal position within Azhdarchidae, though a full phylogenetic analysis was not performed due to fragmentary remains, and the precise phylogenetic relationship with other azhdarchids remains unclear as no exact cladistic analysis was initially provided.
